newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Millennium buys stake in tobacco firm.
newsitem.headline: Millennium buys stake in tobacco firm.

text.p: Millennium Group Ltd, formerly Allied Industries International Ltd, said on Monday it had agreed to buy a 25 percent stake in Worldwide Golden Leaf Ltd for HK$264 million.

Millennium said in a statement it would issue 80 million new shares at HK$3.3 each to Golden Leaf owner Yanuar Joeng in return for the stake. The new shares would represent about 8.2 percent of Millennium's enlarged share capital.
Golden Leaf makes, packages, sells and distributes Hongtashan cigarettes, considered one of the leading brands of cigarettes in China, Millennium said.
Yuxi Hongta, a Chinese state-owned enterprise, owns the Hongtashan brand name.

Hongtashan cigarettes sold by Golden Leaf are presently distributed to the United States, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Burma, Cambodia, Nepal and Indonesia. "It is planned that Golden Leaf will market and distribute Hongtashan cigarettes in Hong Kong's retail market in the near future," Millennium said.
Golden Leaf also trades tobacco leaves and acts as an agent to export tobacco and cigarette making and packaging machinery.

"The directors...believe that the association with Yuxi Hongta, one of the largest tobacco companies in the PRC (People's Republic of China), will benefit the company in exploring new investment opportunities in the PRC," Millennium said.
Under the acquisition agreement, Joeng has guaranteed that Golden Leaf's audited net attributable profit for the year ending March 31, 1998 will not be less than US$30 million.
If 1998 profit falls below that amount, Joeng will pay the shortfall either in cash or through more Golden Leaf shares.
Shares in Millennium Group were up HK$0.05 at HK$3.775 in morning trading on Monday.
